The native spin continues, slows near the hand and is phased onto the held heading; only the last fifth blends the hand tilt. The same plan is drawn between 60 Hz ticks. Replaces the speed-chasing homing and the slerp from a fast spin.

Trespasser: the native translucent grey background/frame is drawn again with the rings, nodes and beams (HUD prompts stay hidden). The panel sits just above the plugged prong tip, facing the viewer, instead of 0.55 units above the hand.

Hydrodisplacer: the item update is no longer suspended while plugged (no controller aim when docked had reset it to the reach pose every tick). The native reach, transfer command, cutaway and withdraw run. During the native water cutaway the headset rides the authored camera glide, level, between its two black fades.

Bolt cranks: the open jaws of the original crank pose (sequence 0xb) straddle the hex head, centred on the bolt axis at the head mid-height, as in Ratchet's native 1.05-ring crank poses measured from the assets. The shaft points to the hand with a bounded tilt and lengthens about the jaws.

Hoverboard: on mounting and on each teleport of the board (start, crash and wrong-way respawns), the current gaze becomes the board's heading, as a recentre does; the board steers toward the gaze, so a player who walked up from the far side rode backwards.

Taxis and carriers (Rilgar's hover cars, Kerwan's transports, ferries, path platforms): no room-scale step while the carrier's edge brake or jump lockout is set; the car's wall only exists inside the tick, so a physical step pushed Ratchet over the edge.

The reticles, drawn by the game at the screen centre (Gaspar's marker FX 0xd, Hoven's and Batalia's HUD reticles), mark where the guns point.

culling_turrets_scenes.reported_behavior: The Hoven arrival cutscene overlooks the level from far away; cutscenes should start facing where Ratchet looks; turret fights (Hoven especially) are unpleasant, often not at the turret's centre, worse than on PS2; the ship disappears right after the inter-planet loading lag until the next screen; scenery outside the camera is missing in VR in in-level movies, ship take-offs / landings / boarding and the Visibomb view.
changes: Culling for the headset: tfrags, ties, shrubs and mobys are culled and LOD-picked for the headset's eye in every mode (the native camera, an authored shot in movies, ship sequences and the Visibomb view, was used there); while the native image is shown too (the Visibomb's monitor, a gadget's panel) anything either view draws is drawn; the Visibomb's short draw-distance caps no longer apply to the headset's view. The game's 'drawn last frame' (+0x31) that gameplay reads keeps the native camera's culls.
Cutscenes start facing where their actor looks: the head's heading at the scene's start becomes the direction of Ratchet's (or Clank's) head joint.

Scenes with no one to see through (the infobot's messages, flyovers): a spectator view at the scene's camera, its heading taken at the start and at each cut, the head free. A scene no longer reuses the previous scene's eye (Hoven's arrival was seen from Orxon's last eye position), and a pilot view hands over its anchor.

Turrets (Gaspar's cannons, Hoven's and Batalia's turrets): the eye sits at the turret's seat (Gaspar's camera pivot, 3 up on Hoven's axis, above Batalia's barrels), anchored when mounting, the view fixed while the turret turns beneath it and set facing its aim; the turret turns toward where the right controller points (the gaze without it, the stick while pushed) at its own speeds without overshooting (Batalia's yaw acceleration and pitch speed raised for a pointing hand); the trigger fires; no wrench while manned.
The ship after an inter-planet loading: the new level's setup no longer hides the flight's kept actors (their mesh tag 0 matched the hero's instance), so the ship stays visible through the swap.
culling_turrets_scenes.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check and Windows debug build passed. No tests, gameplay scripts or headset session were run.
culling_turrets_scenes.remaining_confirmation: In-level movies, ship take-offs / landings / boarding and the Visibomb view with nothing missing (and the frame rate there); cutscene start orientation; Hoven's arrival scene as a spectator; the three turrets (seat, aiming with the controller, firing); the ship through the inter-planet loading.

vr_options_helmet.reported_behavior: In cutscenes where Ratchet wears the O2 Mask it follows his head and hides the view; in play we cannot tell we wear it. Wanted: a VR Options page below Port Options with Helmet and Boots toggles (both on by default); a shown helmet follows the player's head and is seen through its visor, in play and in in-level movies; shown boots at our feet. Also: on Oltanis no weapon, gadget or wrench is drawn although they work.
changes: VR Options page (only with a VR headset), right below Port Options in the pause menu's and the main menu's Options: Helmet and Boots, On or Off, On by default, saved in the port settings file (vr_helmet / vr_boots). The port page code serves both pages (rows per list widget).

The worn helmet (the O2 Mask or the Pilot's Helmet) is drawn on the player's head in play, in Ratchet's scenes and in the ship sequences: placed from the headset so that the eye sits behind its visor (measured on the model: the visor's alpha texels, the eye 0.15 from the shell), in its bind pose; the scene's and the ship actor's own helmet is hidden. Off: no helmet at all.
The worn boots are drawn at the hidden body's feet as the game poses them (the VR hand presentation no longer hides the worn items); Off hides them.

Oltanis (and every arrival without a landing after a flight streamed in VR): the travel's hide flag is cleared, so the hand items are drawn again (it stayed set because the preloaded switch skips level_unload's reset).
vr_options_helmet.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check and Windows debug build passed. No tests, gameplay scripts or headset session were run.
vr_options_helmet.remaining_confirmation: The VR Options page and its persistence; the O2 Mask / Pilot's Helmet on the head in play, in scenes (Orxon, Gemlik) and in the ship sequences (visor tint, the HUD behind the shell); boots at the feet; hand items on Oltanis.

reach_flip_visor.reported_behavior: Clank's antenna halo is 20-30 cm off; boots about 1 m ahead on grind rails (mines hard to hit there); the take-off camera leaves the ship; the O2 Mask's view is narrow and its visor too opaque; the inter-planet loading hitch; the wrench should reach further as the native swing stretches it; the Hyper Strike's native aim assist; a Hyper Strike on a crate stack sometimes grabs its top; a 'Camera flip' VR option (off by default); two-handed weapons heavier in one hand.
changes: Clank's antenna dot (drawn on the hidden body's back) is never drawn in VR.

Rails: the eye predicts the body (the last tick plus its velocity over the overstep) instead of trailing it with a smoothing lag: the eye, the hands and the wrench's hits were 1-1.5 m behind the body at grind speed; the prediction fades out after the rail.
Take-off: once Ratchet sits down, the eye is the ship's seat, from the pose the hull is drawn with (his own track is authored apart from the ship's and drifted out of it).

O2 Mask / Pilot's Helmet: the eye sits closer behind the visor (0.16 forward) and the helmet is 15 % taller about the eye, for a wider view through it; the visor glass (only the texels under the alpha test) is drawn at 60 % of its alpha (37.5 % opacity).
Wrench reach: a fast swing stretches the drawn wrench up to 35 % (1.0 to 3.5 m/s), as the native swing sequences stretch its head; the hit sweep reaches out with it.

Hyper Strike: the native aim assist's target carries to a physical wrench (the falling body drifts toward a target within 2.5, and a strike missing it by less than 0.75 is pulled onto it); the gesture needs a mostly downward stroke of 8 cm at 1.6 m/s, its cooldown is 0.3 s and the frame's swing hit no longer lands on top of it.
Crates: the hand holding the wrench does not grab a ledge on a crate (a crate stack's top), nor any ledge while a Hyper Strike is pending.

Camera flip (VR Options, off by default, saved as vr_camera_flip): the view turns with Ratchet's head joint during flips, double jumps, wall jumps and grind jumps (faded in and out, interpolated per tick); the aim, the hands and the walking direction keep the upright root.
Two-handed weapons held in one hand lag in turn (0.22 s) and position (0.12 s, at most 10 cm), droop 6 degrees and sag 1.5 cm; with the support grip they follow exactly (not the Hydrodisplacer).

Inter-planet loading: the destination's item tables come from the per-level cache (no boot ELF re-read on the main thread), the departure world is freed on a worker thread at the cut, and the swap logs its phases (VR_HITCH) for the next step.
reach_flip_visor.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check and Windows debug build passed. No tests, gameplay scripts or headset session were run.
reach_flip_visor.remaining_confirmation: No antenna dot; boots under you and wrench hits on rails; the take-off view in the seat; the O2 Mask's view and tint; wrench reach; the Hyper Strike's aim and the crate stacks; the Camera flip option; one-handed two-handed weapons; the loading hitch (and the VR_HITCH timings).

direction_walloper.reported_behavior: A VR option for the character's orientation following the gaze or the body (hands + head), body by default; the wrench should whoosh when swung, even in the air; Clank's antenna light is still offset in in-level movies; Giant Clank feels like the model's orientation is independent of how we are turned; with the Walloper the grip does not switch back to the wrench; the Walloper misses consecutive punches while the arm moves; the quick select blocks the character's movement.
changes: VR Options 'Direction': Body (default) or Gaze, saved as vr_direction. Body: the heading and the stick's frame follow an estimate from the head and both controllers (the shoulder line, the hands' midpoint ahead of the head, where the controllers point), following past 15 degrees and settling within 2 so a glance does not swing it, the head never more than 90 degrees from it, the head alone when a controller is untracked.
The wrench whooshes on each physical swing (the native combo swings' sound markers, sequences 3..5 in turn), hit or miss, once per stroke.
Glow billboards face the headset's eye in every mode (in scenes they faced the authored shot's camera and were pulled sideways: Clank's antenna light).

Giant Clank: his heading follows the player in every gameplay state but death (his missiles and beam kept the heading from when the trigger was pressed); his missiles leave from the hand drawn on that side's controller.

Walloper: a still grip (no lunge, 9 ticks) takes the wrench back; punches re-arm when the stroke slows below half its peak or the arm pulls back, a punch thrown during a lunge chains once its hit window is over, the cooldown is 0.22 s, and the trigger's native lunge no longer disables physical punches.
Quick select: the left stick keeps moving Ratchet (the right hand picks); the ring's pad lock is lifted and the stick's d-pad bits are kept out of the ring.
direction_walloper.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check and Windows debug build passed. No tests, gameplay scripts or headset session were run.
direction_walloper.remaining_confirmation: The Direction option (Body / Gaze); the wrench's whoosh; Clank's antenna light in scenes; Giant Clank's missiles and beam; the Walloper (grip back to the wrench, consecutive punches); walking during the quick select.

strafe_walloper.reported_behavior: No sound on the wrench's swings; the Walloper sometimes takes false backward inputs, especially while walking backward, and fires when the arm folds back, sending Ratchet the opposite way from where the player looks; walking backward or sideways does not really exist in the original game, where Ratchet and Clank always move the way they face, and should be implemented properly.
changes: The wrench's whoosh is Ratchet's own class sound 27, the marker on his native swing animations (the wrench's swing sequences carry no sound marker, so nothing played): once per fast stroke, hit or miss.

Walking backward and sideways: the native movement physics (turn spring, speed rules, running jump and its push, air control, wall, step and edge probes) run with the hero facing the way he moves (the stick, or the motion carried once it is released while he still has speed); the player's heading comes back right after the move, for the transitions, flips, weapons, aim, ledges and the drawn hands. Ratchet idle, walk, stop, crouch, fall, jumps, double jump, water jump and wading; Clank and the Hologuise idle, walk and fall. A walk keeps only the motion along the stick (a reversal starts from rest); the running jump and the step down follow the motion; Clank's landing no longer stops on a stick off his heading.
In VR the stick walks and no longer aims the wrench states, the Walloper or the Hyper Strike (their aim and target search follow the player's heading).

Walloper punches: the right hand's motion relative to the head (walking or leaning is not a punch), at least 1.45 m/s, within about 55 degrees of the player's facing and away from the spine; an arm folding back, a sideways swing or a backward step never punches. The lunge goes where the player faces, turned at most 25 degrees toward the punch or the trigger's aim; Ratchet faces it during the lunge, and the windup keeps only the motion along it.
strafe_walloper.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check and Windows debug build passed. No tests, gameplay scripts or headset session were run.
strafe_walloper.remaining_confirmation: The wrench's whoosh; walking backward and sideways (no forward lurch on release, jumps, steps, walls); Walloper punches only forward, the lunge along the facing.

streamed_loading.reported_behavior: The inter-planet loading hitch: the swap frame took 170-225 ms on the main thread (VR_HITCH startup 120-180 ms, unload 13-27 ms, despawn 11-33 ms) and the render thread then stalled about 100 ms uploading the whole level (prep up to 93 ms).
changes: The loader thread prepares the level start beside the load (crate::level_switch::PreparedLevel): the tfrag batches, tie, shrub and moby class meshes, their images, the tie and shrub instance records and entity lists (names included). The boot uses the same path; the title world and Going Commando build theirs in place.

A VR flight streams the destination (crate::level_stream): meshes and images get their handles at the swap and are inserted at most 4 MiB, 12 images and 48 meshes per frame; tie and shrub entities are spawned within 2.5 ms per frame, the tie LOD state naming each instance's entities as they come.

At the swap the old ties are hidden and despawned a few hundred per frame; the level's unloaded resources, the replaced Level, fog and spawn states and the old level's lumps are freed on a cleanup thread (every level change).
The voyage may finish only once the stream is empty and the destination uploaded; a new level change first completes a stream still running.

VR_HITCH stream (what was streamed, frames, job time) and VR_HITCH frame (any main or render frame of 20 ms or more during a transition, with its phase and its time per main schedule); VR_PERF main now includes the level change's frame; `level setup:` times the set-ups of a level's first frame (gameplay step by step, Ratchet's attachments, the menus' 3D models, the vendor).

A flight streaming the destination leaves the gameplay set-up, Ratchet's attachments, the menus' 3D models and the vendor for the cut to the landing, under black; the voyage (travel post_tick), the VR camera (follow_game_camera) and the flight's audio use the departure's play state until then, and the pipeline warm-up view is the level's Ratchet instance.
streamed_loading.measured: Headset, 2026-10-25. Kerwan to 08 / 08 to 01 (first build): change frame 34-41 ms (was 170-225 ms), then one frame of 142-162 ms (menus' 3D models 62, gameplay 31, attachments 24, vendor 5, menus 4). Kerwan to 10 (final build, set-ups at the cut): change frame 40 ms, the next frames at most 27 ms, upload 35 MiB over 52 frames; worst flight frame about 245 ms before this branch, 40 ms now.
streamed_loading.validation: Non-VR cargo check, VR cargo check, clippy (no new warning) and the Windows release build passed. The branch's package applied to a fresh upstream checkout reproduces the build checkout exactly. The final build was flown in the headset (Kerwan to level 10) and confirmed by the user; no tests or gameplay scripts were run.
streamed_loading.remaining_confirmation: Pausing during a flight after the level change (the destination's play state is not set up yet); longer play after landing on more destinations (vendors, the pause pages' 3D preview).
